overview: The two main types of blood vessels, distinguished mainly by direction of blood flow and wall structure, not by the type of blood carried.
genZNote: Arteries: blood leaving the heart, high pressure, thick walls. Veins: blood heading home, low pressure, valves included.

aspects.label: Direction of Blood Flow
aspects.valueA: Carries blood away from the heart.

aspects.label: Wall Thickness
aspects.valueA: Thick, muscular, and elastic walls to withstand high pressure.
aspects.valueB: Thinner walls with less muscle, since pressure is lower.

aspects.label: Presence of Valves
aspects.valueA: Generally no valves (except semilunar valves at the heart's exit).
aspects.valueB: Contains valves to prevent backflow, especially in limb veins.

aspects.label: Oxygen Content
aspects.valueA: Usually carries oxygenated blood (exception: pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood).
aspects.valueB: Usually carries deoxygenated blood (exception: pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood).

overlay.examHighYieldNote: The pulmonary artery and pulmonary vein are the classic exception to the 'arteries = oxygenated' rule — direction of flow, not oxygen content, defines an artery vs vein.
overlay.memoryTrick: Arteries Away from heart. Veins back toward the heart (think 're-Vein' for return).
overlay.commonMisconception: Blood type (oxygenated vs deoxygenated) does not define artery vs vein — direction of flow relative to the heart does.
